findings.text: the fragment says each of the three migrated readers "reproduces its base-revision output on all six inputs", which the node's own table contradicts - tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py:201 records four changed cells of the repository-clock reader (empty, malformed, naive and non-string) and the module docstring at :11 says three of the four readers reproduce every cell - so a reader of the fragment alone concludes no behaviour moved.

parse_utc is applied to str(stamp) where the base revision called datetime.fromisoformat, so the budget-hold evidence stamp now accepts whitespace-padded ("  2026-09-29T01:02:03Z ") and lowercase-z stamps that the base read as "the evidence age is unknown" (probe of both scratch trees: base unknown, head -0.0/62.0 minutes old) and _lane_advisory_instant at :2592 widens the same way for lowercase z, while the manifest's evidence_inputs says only four cells of the repository-clock reader move and the table's input list carries neither shape.

baseline_suite and after_suite both carry unsubstituted placeholders in their command fields ("<92 files>", "PYTHONPATH=<worktree> ... <92 files + tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py>"), so neither arm can be re-run from the record, and the file list is recorded nowhere else either: my AST scan finds 40 tests/ files importing reckon.crew.dispatch at base, which the 92-file selection plausibly covers but the record cannot show.

the head arm's revision line names the base sha fdb116e2 and describes its tree as "working tree with node C and one commit", the manifest's after_suite names 46d18cc5, and the only revision the log itself names is bc811c64 in a correction appended after 2,072 lines of output, so tying the 34-failure measurement to the committed head rests on a trailing note plus an out-of-band check that bc811c64 and 46d18cc5 share tree 85e4033e.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit - 46d18cc5 routes three of the four readers through reckon._timestamps and adds the 29-test table, f21c48fb adds the fragment; nothing outside the three readers changed in the module, and the retained fromisoformat carries a comment at :2749 stating why in mechanism terms.
item_verdicts.done_when: one fromisoformat hit remains in reckon/crew/dispatch.py (:2754, pinned by the AST guard at tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py:177) and it is named as the retained exception with its differing input at :193, the six-row per-reader table exists and passes 29/29 in my own run at the committed head, both arms end with an EXIT= line and both basetemps are deleted, but the head arm adds three failing ids the base arm does not, all three of which pass serially at both trees (I re-ran each side myself).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is the four timestamp readers in reckon/crew/dispatch.py reading through reckon._timestamps keeping their current results; :401 and :413 now call parse_utc, :2592 calls parse_iso, and the fourth reader is the retained exception the fence names; my 19-input probe of both scratch trees reproduces every recorded cell of all four readers, though :401 and :2592 widen two shapes the base revision refused (FINDING).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the logs it names exist and carry what it states (base-arm.log 31 failed/1011 passed EXIT=1, head-arm.log 34 failed/1037 passed EXIT=1, negative-control.log 1 failed/28 passed), its rewrite note checks out because bc811c64's tree hash equals 46d18cc5's, but both suite commands carry unsubstituted placeholders and the head log's revision line names the base sha (FINDING).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff fdb116e2..f21c48fb touches exactly the three declared paths (reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes/dispatch-timestamps-reuse-the-parser.html), the declared figures directory is unused, and the worktree is clean at f21c48fb.

justifications.durability: the table at tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py:144 asserts literals recorded from the base revision and the AST guards at :177 and :181 redden if a reader is reverted or a new fromisoformat appears, and I reinstated the declared mutation on my own scratch copy of head to redden exactly the lane offset row (1 failed/28 passed); the table's input list omits the padded and lowercase-z shapes whose behaviour moved.
justifications.evidence: the gate measures the fence's clauses - the table passes 29/29 at head in my re-run, both arm logs carry their EXIT= line with the results the manifest states, and both basetemps are gone - but neither suite command records the file list it ran, so the arm cannot be rebuilt, and the head log names the base sha on its revision line.
justifications.fit: the change reuses the landed shared parser, keeps the module's private-helper idiom and policy docstrings, and states the retention reason at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2749 with no plan, ticket or author identifiers.
justifications.goal_fidelity: three of the four readers at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:401, :413 and :2592 resolve through reckon._timestamps and my 19-input probe of base fdb116e2 and head f21c48fb reproduces every recorded cell, but :401 and :2592 newly accept whitespace-padded and lowercase-z stamps the base revision read as unreadable, which neither the manifest nor the fragment records.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff fdb116e2..f21c48fb is exactly the three declared paths with the declared figures directory unused, and no unrelated edit in reckon/crew/dispatch.py beyond the three readers and the retained-exception comment.
